reuse.why: Adds one assertAccountIsOpenForBankLinking helper used by every link path, but does not attach it to the existing pre-link guard pattern (the app.method wrappers that already run assertBankAccountIsNotLinked before each link).

duplication.why: The closed-account rule is written once; only the one-line call is repeated in five link functions, mirroring the existing per-provider guard repetition.

placement.why: The existing link refusal runs in the handler registrations before the link function, while the new refusal is placed as the first line inside each link function body, so the two pre-link checks live in different layers.

scope.why: Only the helper, its five calls and tests.

maintainability.why: Clear, small helper with the exact error; a new provider has to remember both the registration guard and the in-body call, since the checks are not gathered in one pre-link step.

bypasses_abstraction.where: Every link function (Fintegra through linkSimpleFinAccount) calls assertAccountIsOpenForBankLinking; none re-implements it.

disguised_duplication.where: No duplicated logic; only repeated one-line calls to the new helper.

one_place.where: assertAccountIsOpenForBankLinking in server/accounts/app.ts defines the closed-account refusal, and the GoCardless, SimpleFin/Fintegra, Pluggy.ai, Akahu and Enable Banking link functions all call it.
